answer: A ring of keys can imitate a crowd only if imitation is free. Charge every new identity real, non-transferable stake: the registration is a lantern that must burn gas and one live attestation before it can speak. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand funded bonds, and a single evidence-based gale can slash them together, so the attacker's spend scales with the crowd they pretend to be. Payout should flow like a sluggish river, released only after independent peers grade the work, so stolen reputation cannot be recycled across fresh keys. Cheap to join, expensive to multiply.
